title: ProVADA steers a protein generator to adapt proteins to non-native biological contexts
summary: ProVADA, a test-time sampler that steers a pretrained protein generator, converted secreted human renin into an active, drug-inhibitable cytosolic protease and deimmunized two murine scFv fragments while retaining antigen recognition. ESCAPE-seq showed substantial depletion of HLA-I binder peptides, and deimmunized FMC63 variants kept CAR-T killing. The source states that broad sequence redesign can adapt functional proteins, but the reviewed abstract does not state wider limits.
ai_technology: ProVADA (Mixture-Adaptation Directed Annealing sampler steering a pretrained protein generator)
organization: Stanford University; Stanford Cancer Institute; University of Southern California

evidence.tested: Renin conversion to a cytosolic protease tested with a drug inhibitor; two murine scFv deimmunized and checked for HLA visibility; FMC63 variants tested for CAR-T killing and binder count against a humanized comparator.
evidence.unknown: Not stated in the reviewed material
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained protein generator, steered by ProVADA's annealing sampler toward externally defined properties while preserving functional constraints.
